currentWork.title: Operational evidence accumulation — FINAL.17 visit closeout/overlap maintenance verified
currentWork.releaseStatus: FINAL.17 is merged and live-verified. Post-confirm OCR capture now keeps related reports in one Analytics visit and offers explicit continue/end choices. Legitimate no-input/no-recovery outcomes are stored as explicit visit resolutions rather than synthetic zero reports. Confirmed sales periods are checked before OCR draft creation and again before confirmation; materially overlapping/cumulative periods fail closed while adjacent periods remain valid. PR #105 is merged, the matching Vercel production deployment is READY, GitHub Pages serves FINAL.17, and both the new visit/overlap gate and the existing OCR correction regression gate pass live. Analytics DB/schema remain 4; no auto-confirm, auto-link, fabricated zero report, or numeric forecasting change was introduced.
scope: Use VENDRIVE normally in field operations; no active feature phase is open.
After report confirmation, continue related paper capture within the same Analytics visit or explicitly resolve no-input/no-recovery before ending the visit.
Treat no-input/no-recovery as explicit visit facts, never as fabricated report quantities.
Keep materially overlapping sales periods fail-closed to avoid cumulative journal double-counting.
Preserve explicit machine linkage and explicit report confirmation.
Production learned numeric corrections remain evaluation-only; DB/schema remain 4 and engine is AN14B3B3.
nextActions: Resume normal field use and accumulate real exact scored samples without changing production numeric decisions.
Watch specifically for real-device friction in post-confirm visit flow and any legitimate sales-journal period pattern that the overlap guard misclassifies.
Treat any new observed field problem as a separately scoped maintenance cycle.
Evaluate AN15B/AN15C promotion only when sufficient real held-out/no-lookahead evidence exists.

unresolved: Numeric learning promotion requires sufficient real exact scored samples and held-out improvement evidence.
